hits.title: Ask HN: What are some tips for handling a late invoices
hits.author: failedbyfear
hits.story_text:
I've been working with a startup for several months. Initially things were going well, but an investor backed out at the last minute a couple months ago. At that point they stopped paying contractors and are 60 days overdue on invoices for several people (including me).

They are still paying the employees and they still have a bunch of work that they want me to do. I don't mind helping out and am willing to "loan" them some money if they start paying me for future work. The COO and controller have been ignoring my emails and calls about payment.

Unfortunately I did not put any clauses on my invoices about due dates or late payment fees.

Has anyone had success in working through this type of situation or is it best to just write them off and walk away?

hits.title: What to do when the client is 2 days late on payment?
hits.author: Apane
hits.story_text:
So, I've issued the invoice last Monday, it is now the following Monday. Bare in mind, there is a clause in the contract that states they have 5 days to pay the invoice otherwise they will be charged additional percentage per day late.

The invoice was due to be paid on Saturday, and they are two days late. On the Saturday I sent them a reminder that the payment was due - and I've also just sent a notice that the payment is late, and if there is anything I can do to assist them in making the payment.

I haven't received a response yet - any ideas on what I should do in this case? I've had no problems with them before but I'm getting a bit worried as this is un-like them.

Thanks!

hits.title: Tired of chasing clients for late payments
hits.author: jesusfchristn
hits.story_text:
Each month there is at least one client who does not pay my invoice.

I absolutely despise sending follow up reminders it feels needy, awkward, and just a reframing of mental energy.

So, I am thinking...what if an AI tool could send those reminders for me?

Connect to Stripe or PayPal, it predicts who will likely pay late and automatically sends out a reminder email that gets firmer each time.

IM NOT selling anything. Just qualifying if this is a pain point. Would you actually be willing to pay $49/mo for it to manage this whole mess for you? Or is this just a nice idea? And it's not worth cash?

Only be brutally honest please :)

hits.title: Show HN: Delfyn, AI Agent to help businesses get paid faster
hits.author: jhack88
hits.story_text:
Hi HN,

I'm Junior, founder of Delfyn, and I’ve been building an AI-powered agent that helps finance teams get paid on time. If you've ever dealt with slow-paying B2B customers, broken invoice matching, or cash flow uncertainty, this might resonate.

The problem: In B2B, waiting 60–90 days to get paid is common. AR teams spend hours manually:

- Reconciling payments to invoices

- Chasing customers

- Updating spreadsheets

Explaining why cash flow projections keep being wrong

Meanwhile, late payments quietly bankrupt 1 in 4 SMEs in Europe.

What Delfyn does: We built an AI agent that helps automate:

Invoice-to-payment matching using rules, embeddings (e.g. “0099” → “INV-2023-0099”), and retrieval models

Cash flow forecasting with transaction-level granularity

Proactive reminders + incentive recommendations to reduce DSO

We're combining deterministic logic (amount, IBAN, date) with semantic models (e.g. e5-base-v2) and LLMs (for gray-zone explanations only).

Who it's for: Finance teams (esp. in B2B SaaS, agencies, professional services)

Founders managing AR themselves

Companies tired of relying on NetSuite exports + wishful thinking. Or even worst sending payments collections emails to customers who have already paid. I've seen that a lot.
